title: Weak point Wednesday: lower abs
summary: NH covers lower abs as his weak point. Ab count (4, 6, 8) is genetic, and lower abs show last because men store fat near the waist; dieting helps, but since he isn't cutting he focuses on developing the muscle. He does daily hanging leg and knee raises with a controlled negative and stretch at the bottom, plus weighted floor leg raises; his favorite is decline-bench crunches, which he replaces with assisted dragon flags for sets of 10 since the bench costs about $800.

claims.claim: Abs are one of the most genetically unfair muscle groups: you can be born with four, six or eight visible abdominals.
Many people who think they have a four-pack actually have a six-pack that is not developed or lean enough to show.
Upper abs show first because men store more fat around the waist while the area near the ribs stores little fat.
A developed, peeled core is aesthetic regardless of your goal.
The first way to reveal lower abs is diet: less fat on the lower abs makes them visible.
He is losing some fat but not cutting, and is high in body fat, yet his upper abs bulge through because they're very developed; so he focuses on muscular development of the lower abs.
His imbalance comes from spending his first 5 years of training working only the top four abs.
Leg raises from a bar beat floor leg raises because on the floor you feel the hips a lot and don't get the stretch at the bottom.

Hanging leg/knee raises: bring legs up and squeeze, control the negative, let the legs go just past perpendicular to stretch the abs, then use the stretch reflex to pull again; alternate straight-leg and knee raises daily.
He complements hanging raises with floor leg raises holding a dumbbell.
His favorite lower ab exercise is decline-bench crunches, letting bodyweight stretch the abs at the bottom.
A good ab bench costs at least $800 and takes space; he only buys expensive equipment he'll use often or for many exercises.
He substitutes assisted dragon flags: lying on a bench gripping a barbell, he lowers through the negative, then does a momentum leg raise at the bottom to stretch and return, for sets of 10.
